legend: Mrs. Smith is trying to contact her husband, John Smith, but she forgot the secret phone number!
The only thing Mrs. Smith remembered was that any permutation of n%%ZSMJ0%% can be a secret phone number. Only those permutations that minimize secret value might be the phone of her husband.
The sequence of n%%ZSMJ1%% integers is called a permutation if it contains all integers from 1%%ZSMJ2%% to n%%ZSMJ3%% exactly once.
The secret value of a phone number is defined as the sum of the length of the longest increasing subsequence (LIS) and length of the longest decreasing subsequence (LDS).

A subsequence ai1,ai2,…,aik%%ZSMJ4%% where 1≤i1<i2<…<ik≤n%%ZSMJ5%% is called increasing if ai1<ai2<ai3<…<aik%%ZSMJ6%%. If ai1>ai2>ai3>…>aik%%ZSMJ7%%, a subsequence is called decreasing. An increasing/decreasing subsequence is called longest if it has maximum length among all increasing/decreasing subsequences.

For example, if there is a permutation [6,4,1,7,2,3,5]%%ZSMJ8%%, LIS of this permutation will be [1,2,3,5]%%ZSMJ9%%, so the length of LIS is equal to 4%%ZSMJ10%%. LDS can be [6,4,1]%%ZSMJ11%%, [6,4,2]%%ZSMJ12%%, or [6,4,3]%%ZSMJ13%%, so the length of LDS is 3%%ZSMJ14%%.
Note, the lengths of LIS and LDS can be different.
So please help Mrs. Smith to find a permutation that gives a minimum sum of lengths of LIS and LDS.
input: The only line contains one integer n%%ZSMJ15%% (1≤n≤105%%ZSMJ16%%) — the length of permutation that you need to build.
output: Print a permutation that gives a minimum sum of lengths of LIS and LDS.
If there are multiple answers, print any.
note: In the first sample, you can build a permutation [3,4,1,2]%%ZSMJ17%%. LIS is [3,4]%%ZSMJ18%% (or [1,2]%%ZSMJ19%%), so the length of LIS is equal to 2%%ZSMJ20%%. LDS can be ony of [3,1]%%ZSMJ21%%, [4,2]%%ZSMJ22%%, [3,2]%%ZSMJ23%%, or [4,1]%%ZSMJ24%%. The length of LDS is also equal to 2%%ZSMJ25%%. The sum is equal to 4%%ZSMJ26%%. Note that [3,4,1,2]%%ZSMJ27%% is not the only permutation that is valid.

In the second sample, you can build a permutation [2,1]%%ZSMJ28%%. LIS is [1]%%ZSMJ29%% (or [2]%%ZSMJ30%%), so the length of LIS is equal to 1%%ZSMJ31%%. LDS is [2,1]%%ZSMJ32%%, so the length of LDS is equal to 2%%ZSMJ33%%. The sum is equal to 3%%ZSMJ34%%. Note that permutation [1,2]%%ZSMJ35%% is also valid.
